Let me enter your soul, and I’ll awaken your wolf.
Alpha Damon, you’ve got it wrong. I don’t have a wolf. I’m just a slave.
A wolfless girl wouldn’t smell like you. This scent belongs only to a she-wolf.
Since the moment I smelled you, you’ve been haunting my mind.
Just then Damon sees the marks on her body.
Someone made sure you could never discover what you are. Who did this to you?
I can’t tell you. They’ll kill me if I speak
Not if I kill them first.” “Tell me who they are. Give me the names.
But before the girl could say another word, she vanishes.. 
And the dream breaks…
Damon wakes up, breath uneven, his body covered in sweat.
It always ends there. But night after night, the same girl returned with the same wounds.
Fear and the same desperate plea for help.
Please help me Alpha Damon had never bowed to beauty
or cared for desire. The most feared Alpha in the realm. Stopped sleeping. Stopped eating. Her screams followed him even after waking. At first, Damon believed the dreams were a curse.
Until one day he was patrolling the woods and chanced upon a seer.
Her white eyes locking on to him like she had been waiting.
She told him the girl in his dreams was real fated to be his mate,
and that she was suffering. Damon froze for the first time in months. His heartbeat stumbled.
Who is she? Your fated mate.
The words hit him like a blade to the chest. Damon had never cared for the idea of mates.
Never wanted one. Yet the girl haunted him more than war ever had.
Tell me where she is. You will recognize her by her violet glowing eyes,
eyes that hold divinity. Then she vanished.
From that moment, Damon searched.
He crossed territories questioned alphas,
raided underground auctions believing she may have been sold.
Followed every rumor about imprisoned Omegas, searched villages
yet found nothing Until he was summoned
to the Red Moon Pack for an alliance marriage
with Marcy, the daughter of Alpha Edward.
Edward Damon accepted because the moment he heard Red moon pack, his wolf stirred inside him. But the moment he entered the Grand Hall of the Red moon pack, everything changed.
The faint freesia scent lingered in the grand halls of the Red moon pack, but before he could
isolate it, the scent vanished. Something felt wrong. His wolf paced restlessly beneath his skin.
From the moment he entered the territory, His wolf stirred violently. Find her.
The Grand Hall of Red moon overflowed with gold, silk, and false smiles.
Marcy greeted him proudly beside her parents, draped in jewels like she was already Luna.
Damon realized quickly the scent didn't belong to Marcy, but it belonged to someone in the pack, and he would have to play along and show interest in Marcy in order to get closer to his mate.
At that moment, Luna. Layla, Marcy's mother, stepped in, her presence, commanding the room.
Alpha. Damon.
Your room is ready. Please rest. Damon gave a brief nod.
And walked away. But in the kitchen, a very different storm raged.
Marsha's jeweled hand cracked sharply against my face. She hissed. Can't you handle a simple job of serving? Her pride wounded, her control, slipping. Blood spilled from my mouth and pooled onto the kitchen floor. Clean it up. Do You any idea how disgusting your filthy face would look to Alpha Damon? Don't you dare ruin the alliance.
Stay out of sight. Stay invisible.
And remember one wrong move and you'll pay for it.
The princess had always been cruel, but this time it was her wounded
pride that burned hottest. I scrubbed the floor.
Bruises blooming across my knees,
mirroring those already carved into my body. I was spared this time
only because Marcy was in a hurry to attend Alpha. Damon.
But the relief was brief, fragile. Because I knew what came next.
Our next meeting already haunted me. Fear curling tight in my chest. I had no way of knowing.
My fate was about to change. No way of knowing that Alpha Damon, the most powerful pack leader in the realm, had caught my scent.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”
While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.
When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?
Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'
Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled in confirmation. 
He had never expected to hear that word. Never wanted to. And yet, the moment Talia entered the room, something inside him had shifted, changed.
His wolf growled inside him. 'Find her!'
Damon clenched his jaw. "Find her,” He ordered. “Now."
Marcy hesitated, she was confused. Why would an Alpha give a shit about a slave? Damon’s Alpha energy radiated off of her, making her lower her head. "Yes, Alpha Damon."
But Marcy already knew. She’d be doing much more than just finding her… 
Meanwhile, Damon paced, running his tongue over his teeth, irritated beyond reason. His body still ached with unfinished release, but the thought of Marcy’s coconut scent made him recoil. It wasn’t her scent he wanted, it wasn’t her body against his that he needed.
It was her. Talia.
The girl with the smart doe eyes and copper-colored hair.
Damon prowled through the packhouse, inhaling deeply. Nothing. No trace of her scent.
His wolf snarled. 'Find her!'
'If she was really my mate, why did she run? Why didn’t she feel it too?'
'You had another woman on her knees in front of you,' his wolf sneered. 'What did you expect? That she’d throw herself into your arms?'
Damon scowled. His instincts screamed at him to chase, but logic held him back. He needed to stay in control. If he lost control and Marcy found out the truth, there was no telling what they would do to her! 
For now, he would wait.
Later that night, Marcy returned to Damon’s chambers. She couldn't wait to tell him how she put the girl in her place, that wretched, wolf-less slave. But when she saw Damon standing there, Marcy forgot all about the girl.
And she would make him forget all about her too.
But Damon barely acknowledged her, his mind consumed by the memory of that freesia scent.
Marcy advanced, “Hello, Damon.”
Damon swiftly turned toward the door to see Marcy peeking in. He wondered if she even knocked, but even if she did, he probably wouldn't have noticed.
He never felt this distracted!
What if that was an enemy? That copper-haired girl already caused him to be weak, and he didn't even acknowledge their mate bond.
"Why are you here?" Damon asked.
"You look tense..." Marcy said while reluctantly putting her palms on Damon's firm chest. 
"I can help you relax."
Damon's lips lifted into a half-smirk. "And how would you do that?"
"I know that nothing is confirmed, but technically, we are engaged,"
Damon observed her fingers as they moved slightly. 
She felt him out over the thin fabric of his shirt.
He noticed a big ring on her right middle finger, an oval-shaped ruby with small diamonds surrounding it.

"What?"

That intoxicating scent. Sweet citrus and wild temptation. His pulse pounded, his body moving before his mind caught up, drawn to the scent like a predator to prey. His hunt led him to the kitchen, shadow pooling in the corner, the hum of the refrigerator filling the quiet.
And there she was.
A small figure bathed in the cold glow of the open fridge, unaware of the danger lurking just behind her.
Damon closed the distance. Too close. Close enough that his heat ghosted over her nape, close enough that he could imagine how she’d feel beneath him. Soft. His.
"Mhm." His voice came unbidden, dark, possessive.
Talia gasped, jerking back—right into him.

His grip tightened. Rage.
"What happened?" His voice was no longer smooth. It was a blade, sharp with violence.

"Lies." His thumb ghosted over the mark on her cheek. It was shaped like a ring.
Marcy.

Talia shuddered. "No one."
A lie. A plea. A desperate attempt to protect the monster who hurt her.

Then, she did.
Gone. Vanished.
She had run from him again, Damon couldn’t believe it.
Damon stood frozen for a second. Then "Damn it!"
His wolf snarled. Find her.
Damon’s body moved on instinct, chasing the fading scent of freesia into the night.

'If she’s my mate, why didn’t she feel it? She should have wanted to be near me, not running for her life.'

No, his wolf corrected. 'She’s a she-wolf. But for some reason, her inner wolf hasn’t awakened. It could be abuse. Starvation. Or something darker. Maybe… her wolf has been silenced.”
Silenced? Who would do such a thing? What reason could they possibly have to justify such  cruelty? Ripping a wolf from her other half, severing the sacred bond between soul and beast.  Damon couldn’t imagine a fate more brutal. More inhumane.
Damon raked a hand through his hair, his frustration mounting. He’d frightened her. He let her leave without food. And now, she was out there—alone, vulnerable.
'How do I fix this?'
His wolf growled. 'Fix what?

Damon stormed up the stairs, each step heavier than the last. His blood ran hot, his chest tight with frustration he couldn’t shake.
She ran from him.
The copper-haired girl with those wide, frightened eyes and the scent that still clung to his skin. Like she wanted nothing to do with him.

A distraction.
That’s all he needed. That’s all this was.
He closed the door with a snap and stepped toward the bed, gaze dark and unreadable.

Then he grabbed her.
Damon sat on the edge of the bed later, running a hand through his damp hair. The shower hadn’t washed away the frustration, nor the bitter aftertaste of what just happened. Nora was already gone.

Not Marcy’s.
Nora’s.

His wolf sneered. "I warned you. She is the only one who can satisfy us."
Damon growled under his breath. He didn’t want this to be true. He didn’t want to need the girl with the copper-colored hair.
And yet… he did.
If he was ever going to find peace again, he needed to find her.
His frail, elusive mate.
The Omega who kept slipping through his fingers.
The next morning, Damon contacted Caden and Maya through their mind link.
'Are you guys up?'

Maya’s voice grew alert. 'Did something happen?'

That cruel woman. His so-called betrothed. He could tear her apart if it wouldn't start a damn war. Though maybe there were other ways to destroy her…
Caden turned toward the door when Damon’s voice stopped him. “Could you look into Marcy for me? Anything we can use to discredit her: past scandals, secrets, whatever you can find.”

'Are you thinking about rejecting her?' his wolf asked.
Damon sighed. 'I need to protect her.'
'Then keep her close. Don’t reject her.'
His wolf had explained that, without her wolf, Talia didn’t feel the bond. She wasn’t drawn to him the way he was to her. To win her, he’d have to do it the human way; court her, earn her trust.

Damon didn’t know the first thing about romance, but he knew one thing—no one could know she was his mate.
If Alpha Edward learned, he’d use her against him. She’d become leverage, a hostage. Damon couldn’t allow that.
After breakfast, Damon met with Alpha Edward in his office.

Edward bristled. “We provide accommodations, three meals a day. They have access to the kitchen. We train them, discipline them if necessary, but no one is mistreated."

Edward’s eyes sharpened. "Marcy?"

Edward narrowed his eyes. "I’ll speak with her."
Damon smirked. "I’m counting on it."
Later when Marcy entered Edward’s study, he cut straight to the point.
"How is your relationship with Damon?"

Edward’s voice darkened. "Then explain why he thinks you beat Omegas half to death."

Edward’s jaw clenched. "You’d better. Find Damon. Make him yours. By any means necessary."
Marcy rushed to her room, slamming the door shut behind her. Her hands trembled as she braced herself against the vanity. That was close.

After a deep breath, Marcy steeled herself. She wouldn’t fail.
She stripped off her dress, selected something more daring—plunging neckline, fabric that clung in all the right places—and touched up her makeup before making her way to find Damon.
She found him outside his room, speaking with his mated betas Caden and Maya.
"Are you guys going out?" she asked, feigning casual interest.

Damon’s eyes were cold as they landed on her. "Can I help you, Marcy?"

He found out.

She smiled sweetly. "I was hoping we could talk. Just the two of us."
Damon glanced at Caden, who gave him a knowing nod before leading an eye rolling Maya away.

Damon’s gaze swept over her body, unreadable.
"All of it."

As Damon searched the grounds more desperately, he hatched an idea. Damon knew that as a guest he couldn't go anywhere he wanted, so he asked Alpha Edward to assign him an escort.

Yes, she was wondering why he came to the attic.
Did he come to hurt her? Or was this some prank? Since Olivia left the pack, no one came to the attic with good intentions.
That's the scary Alpha who was the reason she got beaten twice. The first time because she looked in when Princess Marcy was between Alpha Damon's legs, and the second time because she complained how Princess Marcy hit her the first time.
Well, the first time she was not watching on purpose, and she definitely didn't complain to anyone, but it didn't matter. She still got beat twice and the only conclusion Talia had was that nothing good ever came from being associated with this big scary Alpha.
And now he was here, in the attic, bringing more misfortune with him.
With every next second of Damon's presence in the attic, Talia sensed a calamity approaching, a calamity in the form of princess Marcy wanting to kill her.
Talia didn't say anything and Damon stepped inside.
She pushed with her legs, getting further into the corner while trying to increase the distance between them.'You are scaring the girl again…', his wolf growled in his head.
Damon lifted his hands, palms facing Talia. "I won't hurt you."'Yeah, you won't hurt me, but others will because of you.', Talia thought.
In slow movements, he closed the door behind him and approached her carefully until his feet touched the edge of the futon.
He went down into a squat so that they were on the same level, but she was still much smaller than he was.
"My name is Damon." He put on his best non-intimidating smile, but she saw it like a beast showing teeth before devouring its prey.
"What's your name?" Damon asked.
Talia's eyes darted to the door and then went back to him.
"Please, leave." She said in a shaky voice, and his heart ached. He finally found her and there was no way he would leave just like that.
Damon was not sure what to do. Why was she so scared? Why was she chasing him away?
"I won't hurt you." He assured her. "I'm here only to talk."
"Say what you have to and leave," Talia said and gestured toward the door, her hand moving enough for the sleeve to hitch higher and expose her swollen wrist.
Damon grabbed her hand and pulled it toward him.
Delightful sparks formed upon contact, catching him by surprise. The sensation was stronger than he remembered, and he inhaled a shaky breath.
He focused mightily on inspecting her injury.
"What happened? Don't tell me that you fell again." His expression darkened. "Is it Marcy? I will teach her a lesson."
Talia panicked. "Please, don't. If you say anything, she will hit me more."
Damon paused and observed her face which was now peeking up above her knees, and he noticed a few more bruises compared to what he saw the previous night.
Rage rippled through Damon at the thought of Talia getting hurt again, and he was right here, in this packhouse, oblivious to her sufferings. It happened on his watch!
Damon was enraged, and his wolf was as well. One fury amplified the other and Damon radiated inexplicable violence that was tangible.
At the sight of Talia shivering in fear, Damon forced his rage down. Settling scores will need to wait.
"Did Marcy hit you again?" Damon asked Talia, and the way she avoided him made him suspect another thing. "Was it because of me?"
Talia's eyes widened and that was enough for him to confirm how his intuition was right.
He knew that Marcy was a white lotus. There was no way Marcy would forget that Talia saw her in a compromising position – between Damon's legs – and when Damon told Alpha Edward that Marcy was hitting Omegas, Marcy probably knew that his comment was about Talia.
In a way, it was his fault that Talia got hurt. Twice.
He clenched his teeth as another wave of rage swelled within him. "I will kill her."
"Don't," Talia pleaded. "Can you just leave and pretend that you didn't see anything? Don't come here and everyone will leave me alone."
Damon's heart cracked. Even if everyone left her alone, how the hell was he supposed to do that?
Didn't she know that he nearly went mad when he didn't know where she was?
Without a word, Damon sat on the futon next to Talia and wrapped her in his arms, pulling her to lean on his chest.
The feeling of Talia against him made Damon's whole body hum in pleasure. Delightful sparks overtook his senses, and he was lost in a daze.
Talia froze. She was not used to physical contact of any kind. It took her a moment to collect herself and start squirming to get out of his hold.
"Shh…" Damon coaxed Talia to calm down, unwilling to let go of her. He was not a hugger, and he never cuddled with a woman, but this girl was different. He wanted to hold her, and her resistance hurt. "I won't harm you. Can I hold you like this, just for a minute?"
No, not a minute. He wanted an hour, or at least until he became immune to these sparks that were making him crave devouring her. But if he said that aloud, she would definitely freak out.
Talia stopped struggling. Not because she agreed, but because she realized that he was too strong, and her struggle made her injuries ache more.
Talia resigned herself to her fate. There was nothing she could do. Even if he wanted to harm her, she could only endure it. She was too weak to fight for herself and if she shouted for help, no one would come.
Damon smirked when he felt that Talia relaxed. He wished to move her to sit on his lap, but he feared that it might be too much.
With his arms around her, Talia appeared tiny and fragile, and Damon was confident that he could carry her around with ease. Or maybe he should stuff her into his pocket, so that she stays close to him all the time.
Lost in the moment, Damon ran his fingers through Talia's coppery-colored hair and inhaled the sweet citrusy scent of freesia, and his world was at peace.
Damon closed his eyes, his enjoyment amplified by the sounds of yips and whimpers his wolf made in pleasure.
"Hey…" Talia called after some time. "When are you going to let me go?"
"First, my name is Damon. Not, hey," Damon said with amusement in his voice. It'd been a while since he heard someone speak to him this casually (other than Caden), but the lack of respect didn't bother him.
"And second…" he drawled, "I'm thinking about it."
If it was up to him, never. To make his point clear, he tightened his hold on her, making sure he didn't crush her. Feeling that she was stiff again, he asked, "Am I hurting you?"
Talia was absolutely confused with this development. "Well… no… but…"
"Then, it's fine." Damon cut her off. He didn't want to hear any buts.
As much as Damon enjoyed this newfound feeling, he couldn't ignore Talia's injuries. The scent of dried blood disturbed the sweet citrusy scent of freesia, telling him that she was not OK.
Damon took Talia's hand in his and observed a cut that was on top of a nasty bruise. It was scabbing, but it still looked fresh.'Mate's healing is slow because she doesn't have her wolf,' Damon's wolf explained.
Damon raised Talia's hand toward his lips and licked the cut.
Talia jerked her hand away, but Damon's reflexes were top-notch, and he increased his grip, preventing her from doing so.
"What are you doing?" Talia asked in panic.
No one ever licked her before, and this was a scary Alpha! Would he eat her?
"Shush! Don't you know that our saliva has analeptic properties? I'm helping your wound heal. You should say, thank you, and not complain." Damon said and grimaced. Considering her sweet scent, he assumed that she would taste sweet also, but… "Why was it bitter?"
"I applied an herbal paste, so it didn't get infected," Talia said in a small voice.
Damon observed her face and noticed that she was beet red. Is she sick?
He touched her forehead. It was not warm, but he still asked, "Do you have a fever?"
"No," Talia responded with urgency. She had no intention to admit she was flustered because a scary Alpha came, hugged her (and was still hugging her!), and then he licked her hand.
Damon guessed that she didn't see a doctor. It was obvious that she didn't get proper first aid.
"Did you make the medicinal paste yourself?"
Talia confirmed with a nod.
He was about to lick her hand again and paused. "Is it poisonous?"
Talia was not sure if she should laugh or cry. "You should ask that before you put things into your mouth."
"I was treating your wound and I didn't see that there was medicine…" He grumbled, and then he licked her again.
"Can you stop doing that?" Talia protested. His coarse tongue touching her skin made her feel funny.
Damon looked at Talia like he had no idea what she was talking about, and then he licked her again.
Talia exhaled helplessly while wondering what game Damon was playing.
He was an important guest, an Alpha, yet instead of mingling with the elite of the Red Moon pack, he was huddled in the corner of the attic, holding her close to him, and licking her hand.
It didn't make sense no matter how she thought about it.
Is this the part where Marcy barged in and they all started laughing at her? Actually, if they only laughed, that would be good. Maybe Damon would join Marcy and the two of them would give her another beating?
Talia was anxious and she wanted this charade to be over.
"When are you leaving?"
Damon was not sure if she asked him about leaving the attic or the Red Moon pack. In either case, his answer would be the same. "Why are you eager to chase me away?"
"Because this is where I stay. You are in a fancy bedroom, with Alpha and Luna, and your future wife."
"My future wife?" Damon asked in confusion, like he heard about it for the first time.
"Princess Marcy told me that you would get married when she came here and…" Talia didn't finish, but Damon understood.
"She will NOT be my wife in this lifetime or in any next one." Damon said grimly.
Talia shook her head. "Maybe you should tell that to her, and not to me. Your relationship with her is not my business. Can you, please, leave?"
Damon was lost in her big honey-colored eyes that looked at him pleadingly and he wondered if he could leave. Could he? Yes, but only in one case.
"Come with me."
Talia was sure that her ears malfunctioned. She asked him to leave the attic before anyone can see them in this inexplicable situation, yet he wants her to join him? "What? Where?"
"I am the Alpha of the Dark Howlers pack. Come with me to my pack."
Talia's brain paused.
She thought that Damon had invited her to his room, to clean up or maybe to make fun of her, but now it seemed he was asking her to leave the Red Moon pack. With him. "Why?"
"I will make sure you have a room, better than the ones downstairs. I will get you clothes that fit, and you can eat anytime you want and as much as you want. For every scratch and bruise, there will be a pack doctor to take care of you and if anyone gives you a hard time, I will deal with them. No one will bully you in my pack."'Our pack!', his wolf added eagerly. Unfortunately, only Damon heard him.
Talia blinked. Now she was not wondering if her ears were tricking her, and if this last beating messed with her brain.
Or maybe something was wrong with him. Did he eat a funny fruit and was talking gibberish? There were some herbs that could make people say things they didn't mean. Or did he confuse her with princess Marcy?
It's not that Talia didn't think about leaving the Red Moon pack. Every time Anna and her henchmen bullied Talia, Talia thought about escaping, but she didn't know where to go. And here was an Alpha, offering her a new home with all the luxuries she ever dreamed of. Assuming that this was real and both of them were sane.
Talia wondered if this was a prank, or if she was imagining this whole conversation, or maybe she was sleeping and the Cinderella story mixed with her dreams because Damon definitely looked like a prince. A handsome prince that smelled of the forest and dark chocolate.
"Will you come with me?" Damon asked when his patience cracked.
"Why do you want me to come?"
"Because…" the words got stuck in his throat.
Could he tell her she was his mate and that when he sees her harmed, his soul aches? No. That would only freak her out.
Could he tell her that staying away from her was practically impossible? If she doesn't come willingly, he would kidnap her or maybe move in with her into this attic. Ah! He sounded like a creep to himself!
Damon was exasperated. All this would be simpler if she could feel the bond and the delicious sparks that make him feel alive.
"Because…" he repeated. "I feel responsible. You got hurt because of me, and it's not right. Let me help you. It will make me feel better." This was the truth. Part of the truth, at least.
"Do you take every girl who gets hurt back to your pack?"
Not really. But he is not the guy who would look away from injustice. However, he couldn't tell Talia that she was special either.
"When you come to the Dark Howlers pack, you will see for yourself that we accept everyone who comes seeking help without bad intentions. I promise that if you don't like it in the Dark Howlers pack, I will help you resettle at the location of your choice."
With his index finger, Damon made a cross over his chest where the heart was, to confirm his sincerity, but his silent promise had an additional clause how he would make sure she was treated well and she never wanted to leave.
Talia bit the inside of her cheek while considering her options.
One was staying at the Red Moon pack. Anna's bullying was escalating, and Marcy started picking on her also. Yesterday Marcy came to the attic and Talia got a beating for something she didn't do.
The second option was to go to the Dark Howlers pack. Alpha Damon said that in his pack people were accepted. Could it be worse than here? Probably not.
Of course, there was also the third option for Talia to leave on her own somewhere, but that option was scary and uncertain, and it will exist even if she goes with Alpha Damon.
Damon saw that Talia was considering it and he spoke with urgency before she could decline his offer. "Grab your things. You only need to say that you reject the Red Moon pack and Edward Redmayne as your Alpha, and the mind link will break. With that, you are free to go, and they can't find you."Talia shook her head. "I don't have the mind link. Alpha Edward's father brought me here as a child, and I never went through the ceremony."
"Good!" Damon exclaimed louder than intended. She doesn't belong anywhere, and he was more than happy to give her a home. With him. "Get your things."
"Just like that?"
Damon nodded. "Just like that."
Talia paused and decided to ask the question that was bothering her from the moment he came to the attic. "How do I know that you are not tricking me?"
Damon stood up and Talia felt chills surround her when his body separated from hers.
He extended his hand toward Talia, palm up. "Let me prove it to you."

  
Now that Damon has found his fated mate, how will he keep her safe?! And what will Talia choose?! Will she trust him?! Stay a slave at the Red Moon Estate? Will she attempt to escape from all of them? What will happen when Edward and Marcy discover Damon has found Talia?!

bodyText:
My daughter-in-law put me on the shuttle bus in Pompeii while the family walked. She told the group it was for my feet. The feet weren't the problem.

I'm fifty-eight. My husband Robert died seven years ago.

My son David got married last year to a woman named Lauren. Lauren is thirty-four and runs the events team at a hotel group in Charlotte. She is, by every measurable standard, a wonderful person. Warm, competent, the kind of woman who remembers your birthday and your mother's birthday and the name of your hairdresser.

Lauren had been planning the Italy trip for ten months. Eight days. Rome, Florence, the Amalfi coast, Pompeii. Twelve of us — David and Lauren, Lauren's parents, her sister and brother-in-law, the kids, and me.

She'd built a spreadsheet. Color-coded. Each day mapped with timing, transport, meal reservations, optional excursions. She'd cc'd everyone.

At the bottom of the spreadsheet was a tab called Mom.

The note said: Mom — Pompeii: shuttle bus from parking lot to amphitheater area. Stairs and ruins difficult. Will meet group for lunch at the café near the entrance.

Stairs and ruins difficult.

I read that twice.

She hadn't asked me. I'd told her, eighteen months ago at the Thanksgiving table, that I was nervous about doing the long walking days in Italy because of my feet — Robert had been the one who used to plan rest stops and pace the days and figure out the cobblestones for me, and I'd lost that. I said it as one comment in a longer conversation. She'd written it down.

She'd been writing things down for a year.

I didn't want a shuttle bus. I wanted to walk Pompeii with the kids. I wanted to figure it out.

I sat with the spreadsheet open at my kitchen island for the rest of the afternoon.

I called my sister Helen that night.

Helen is sixty. Two years ago she walked the Camino de Santiago. Five hundred miles across northern Spain. She'd lost twenty pounds doing it and come back tan and a little smug and obsessively interested in feet.

She's the only person in the family I let myself complain to.

I told her about the spreadsheet. The shuttle tab. The note. The thing I'd said eighteen months ago at the Thanksgiving table.

"Sarah. How are your feet."

"They're fine."

"Sarah."

"They're sixty-year-old feet. They ache by the end of a long day. They were not the reason I was nervous about Italy."

"What was."

I sat with that.

"I don't know. I think I just didn't know how to ask Robert to slow down anymore. And then he was gone. And I didn't know how to be the one who slowed down for myself."

"Right."

"So Lauren put me on a shuttle bus."

"Right."

She was quiet for a second.

"How many pairs of shoes were you planning to bring."

"For Italy. Three. Walking sandals for the cobblestones. A nicer pair for dinners. Some sneakers."

"Cancel all of them. One pair. The walking ones. You walk into that trip in one pair of shoes and you don't change them for eight days."

"Helen."

"I'm serious. The walking days are what you're afraid of. If the shoes are right, the walking days are not the problem. If the shoes are wrong, even the shuttle bus is the problem."

"What pair."

She sent me a link.

"This is what my whole Camino group switched to for the reunion walk next year. We did three weeks on stone in northern Spain and not one of us had a blister. There's a knit version that looks like a normal slip-on — you could wear it to a museum and nobody would think that's a hiking shoe. The front is a lot wider than a normal sneaker. Your toes have room to spread when you push off — which is the whole reason your feet hurt after long days. They're being held together at the front."

"That's not what a podiatrist would tell me."

"It is what a podiatrist would tell you if he walked the Camino. Mine did. He sent me to these."

I looked at the link.

"And they're not orthopedic-looking."

"They're not. They're a slip-on knit shoe. The kind of thing my mother would have called house shoes except they go anywhere."

She was quiet for a second.

"My group ordered together — they had something running where you grab two pairs and the second one is free, so I got the cream and the multicolor for the reunion. The cream sold out two days after we ordered. The colors thin out fast on these and once a color is gone it doesn't come back until next year, if at all."

I ordered the multicolor.

The box arrived four days later.

I opened it at the kitchen island. The shoes were lighter than I expected. The kind of light where you check the bottom of the box to make sure something hadn't been forgotten.

I put them on barefoot. Walked the length of the hallway and back.

The front of the shoe was not where my toes were. My toes had somewhere to go. I stood at the end of the hallway and spread them inside the shoe and felt them spread.

I had not been allowed to do that in any shoe I owned.

In the back of my closet, on the top shelf, was a small leather notebook.

Robert had bought it for me in 1998 on our first trip to Italy. We'd done Rome and Florence over ten days. He'd been forty-three. I'd been forty-two. He'd carried both our bags through Termini Station the day we arrived because mine wasn't going to fit through the turnstile, and he'd insisted.

I'd written sketches and notes in the notebook for the whole trip. The little café where we'd shared a pastry in Trastevere. The view from the dome of the Duomo. The night we'd walked back to the hotel along the river in Rome and I'd taken off my shoes and walked the last block barefoot because my feet hurt and Robert had not said anything, just slowed down to match my pace.

I'd kept the notebook on the top shelf for seven years. I had not opened it since the year he died.

I took it down. I held it. I did not open it. I put it in the inside zip pocket of my carry-on.

Before anything else.

The flight to Rome was overnight.

I landed at Fiumicino at 8 AM with one bag. Through customs in fifteen minutes.

Lauren and David and Lauren's family arrived an hour later on a connecting flight from Munich. They had eleven checked bags between them. I saw Lauren at the baggage claim through the window from where I was sitting at the café, sorting through luggage that had not all made the connection.

The first day in Rome was the Vatican.

Lauren had arranged a wheelchair for me at St. Peter's. Mom — wheelchair available at the entrance, request at the main desk, you don't need to do the lines.

I walked up to the main desk. I thanked the attendant. I told her I wouldn't be needing the wheelchair today.

I did the entire Vatican on my feet. Eleven thousand steps before lunch. The Sistine Chapel. The Pietà. The full route through the museums. The dome.

At the dome — the climb to the cupola, five hundred and fifty-one steps up a tight stone spiral staircase — Lauren's mother stopped halfway. Lauren stopped to be with her. David went the rest of the way up.

I went up too. I came back down. I didn't talk about it.

That night at dinner, Lauren said: "Mom, you've barely sat down all day. Are your feet okay."

"They're fine."

"You can take it easier tomorrow. Pompeii is the long one."

"I'm doing Pompeii."

She blinked.

"The shuttle is already booked, Mom."

"I'll cancel it in the morning."

She looked at David. David didn't say anything.

The next morning at the bus loop in Pompeii, the family was loading onto the walking-tour minibus. The shuttle that Lauren had booked for me was idling on the other side of the parking lot, two retirees from Wisconsin already inside.

I walked past it.

Lauren saw me at the gate of the ruins. She was holding her seven-year-old daughter Emma's hand.

"Mom. What are you doing."

"Walking Pompeii."

"The shuttle —"

"I cancelled it."

Emma looked up at me. "Are you walking with us, Grandma?"

"I'm walking with you, sweetie."

Lauren said nothing. She watched her daughter take my hand.

We walked four hours through the ruins. Emma and I. The whole grid of it — the Forum, the House of the Vettii, the amphitheater, the bath house. I lifted Emma to see over the wall at the amphitheater because she was too short.

At the lunch café, Lauren had reserved a table for the family. We arrived three minutes before everyone else. Lauren's mother was limping slightly. Lauren's brother-in-law was carrying his wife's sandals because the strap had broken on the cobblestones. Lauren was wearing a pair of brown leather sandals — pretty, expensive, the wrong shoe for the day — and her left heel was wrapped in a hotel napkin under the strap.

She looked at my feet.

"What are those."

I told her.

She didn't say anything else.

The next morning, the third day, Lauren's brother-in-law's wife stopped me at the breakfast buffet.

She was in her forties. She'd done her residency at Duke — Lauren had mentioned this once, in passing. I'd assumed she was a hospital doctor.

She said: "I'm a podiatrist."

I looked at her.

"I noticed your shoes yesterday at lunch. The way you were walking. I've been telling patients about these for eight months. Where did you order yours."

I told her. Cloud Walk. By Nimbao.

She nodded. "I bought a pair for my mother in May. She'd had a hammertoe correction done in February and was finding everything too narrow. These were the only thing she could wear without re-aggravating the surgical site. They sold out of the color she wanted within a week of when I ordered."

She paused.

"I'd been wondering whether to recommend them on my practice's social. After watching you walk Pompeii yesterday, I think I'm going to."

She wrote down the name on a hotel notepad.

Florence. Day five. The hill up to Piazzale Michelangelo.

The path goes up four hundred stone steps from the river. It's a steady climb. Tourists do it for the view at sunset.

Lauren had arranged for the family to take a car up.

I walked it.

I walked the four hundred steps with Emma. Halfway up she got tired and I carried her on my hip for thirty steps and then she got off and we walked the rest hand in hand.

At the top, while we waited for the rest of the family to arrive by car, Emma sat on the wall with her legs swinging and watched the city go gold below us.

She said: "Grandma. Are your feet tired."

"A little."

"Mine are too. We did a lot today."

"We did."

She looked at my shoes.

"I want shoes like yours when I'm bigger."

Lauren came up the stairs from the parking lot a few minutes later, walking carefully because the heel of her sandal had come off completely on the ride up. She was carrying it in her hand.

She saw Emma on the wall. She saw me beside her.

She did not say anything.

The last night was on a rooftop in Rome. The family had a private dinner booked at a restaurant near the Pantheon. After dessert Lauren came out to where I was standing at the railing looking down at the lit-up dome of San Salvatore.

She stood next to me for a moment.

"Mom. About Pompeii."

"It's fine."

"It's not fine. I made a spreadsheet and I put you on a shuttle bus and I didn't ask you."

I didn't say anything.

"I thought I was being thoughtful."

"I know."

"And then I watched you walk for eight days."

I waited.

"The shoes, Mom. The ones the podiatrist asked about. Where did you get them. I need to know before we go home."

I looked at her.

"They're called Cloud Walk. Nimbao. Helen ordered them when her Camino group switched."

"And they're still available."

"They do small drops. Helen's group had to move fast — a few colors were already low when I checked back this week. Once a color is gone for the season, it doesn't come back."

She nodded slowly.

"I'd move sooner rather than later if there's one you want."

"Of course."

We stood at the railing for a while longer.

Then she said: "Emma told me she wants a pair like yours when she's bigger."

"I heard her."

Lauren laughed quietly.

"My daughter wants to be sixty-year-old you. I have to recalibrate everything."

I didn't say anything. I let her have that one.

Here's what I learned.

For seven years, since Robert died, I'd been waiting for someone to tell me what I could and couldn't do.

I hadn't realized I was waiting. I just thought I was being careful.

I thought Robert had been the one who knew. He'd handled the maps in Italy, the train tickets, the cobblestones, the slowing-down. After he was gone, I started believing that whoever I lived close to became the one who knew. My son. My daughter-in-law. The doctor at the annual visit who said some swelling is normal at your age.

Lauren put me on a shuttle bus because she'd been listening for eighteen months. She wasn't being cruel. She was being careful, the way I'd taught everyone to be careful with me.

The shoes didn't change my feet.

They changed who got to decide what my feet could do.

If someone has been quietly redrawing your life around what they assume you can't —

If they've planned the shuttle bus and the wheelchair and the rest stop and the easier seat —

If you've started believing the long days are over —

Look at the shoe before you believe any of it.

Not because it solves everything. It doesn't. The cobblestones are still cobblestones. The dome of St. Peter's is still five hundred and fifty-one steps.

But because the moment you realize you've been getting on the shuttle bus on purpose — that's the moment your feet get a vote again.

Helen has the cream pair waiting in her closet for the Camino reunion next year. I'm bringing the multicolor and a second cream — she said her group had that thing running where you can grab two pairs and the second one is free, and I figured I'd give the spare to Emma's mother because she asked.

The cream was nearly gone the morning I ordered. A few colors were already low when I checked back this week.

I'd move sooner rather than later if there's one you want.

I'm planning Greece next year. Emma wants to come.

Your move.

bodyText:
Okay, I need to talk about Disney World. Not the rides, not the churros, not the wait times. The cup situation. Somebody has to.
 
We're a San Antonio family — me, my husband Chris, a seven-year-old, and a four-year-old who negotiates like a hostage negotiator. We did our first Disney trip two years ago and booked this June's trip eighteen months out, because I am that kind of mom and I've made peace with it. I have the lanyard. I have the group — "Disney With Littles," on Facebook, forty thousand of us, do not laugh — and I have a husband with a spreadsheet who says things like "we're burning daylight" at the character breakfast.
 
What I did not have, the first trip, was anywhere to put my water.
 
Nobody tells you this part. Everything else in that park has a solution. There's an organizer for the stroller, a fan that clips to the stroller, a misting bottle, a parade blanket that folds to the size of a taco. I owned all of it. And my forty-ounce Owala — the thing I need most, in a place that is functionally a griddle — had nowhere to live.
 
The stroller cup holder? A lie. It's built for a can of Sprite. My cup sat in it like a linebacker in a kindergarten chair and ejected on the first curb.
 
So the whole first trip, the cup lived in my hand. Or under my arm at the security bag check while I unzipped four compartments one-handed. Or on the ground between my feet in the Dumbo line, where I stood guarding it like a hen because the Magic Kingdom pavement has seen things.
 
At one point — this is real — I handed my phone to my seven-year-old so I could hold the cup and push the stroller, and she took eleven photos of her own thumb and one of a trash can. That's the trip album now.
 
I drank less water in Orlando in June than I do at my desk in an air-conditioned office. Chris got me a Powerade at 4 p.m. on day two because I had a headache, and it cost what Powerade costs at Disney, and we don't talk about it.
 
We got home and I told everyone the trip was magical, which it was, and that my right hand hurt, which it did. I had a claw for a week. Holding a sweating forty-ounce cup for nine hours a day is a repetitive-stress activity. Ask my thumb.
 
And before anybody says "just use a backpack" — I had the backpack. Digging a cup out of a backpack in a moving line while a four-year-old asks if we're there yet is a circus act. The cup needs to be out. Reachable. Cold. Not in my hand. That was the whole spec, and I genuinely did not think the thing existed.
 
This spring, trip two on the calendar, somebody in the group posted: "What's your ONE non-negotiable for summer trips?" Eight hundred comments. Sunscreen. Crocs. The clip fan. One woman wrote "lower your expectations" and got four hundred likes. And then one mom posted a photo of her hip with her cup riding in a little crossbody sling, straw up, and wrote: "This. Hands free since 2025."
 
It's called a Sippy — by Emmafy. I read every reply under that comment like it was a court document. Actually insulated — the kind with layers. Zip pocket that fits a phone. A side pocket, a hook for keys. I ordered one that night — they had a buy one get one free going, so my sister-in-law got the second for the state fair, because different chaos, same physics.
 
Chris said he didn't need anything like that. Remember that.
 
Day one, Magic Kingdom, this June. 96 degrees. Here's the tape:
 
7:40 a.m., security. Nothing in my hands. The bag check line got the stroller and Chris's backpack; mine was one zip, open-shut, done. I walked through like a woman with nothing to declare, because basically I was.
 
9:15, Seven Dwarfs line, fifty-five minutes. Cup on my hip. Phone zipped in the front pocket. I checked our Lightning Lane times one-handed and held my four-year-old's hand the entire line. The entire line. Last trip she held the stroller because Mama's hands were full.
 
11:30, the meltdown. If you know, you know. Goldfish came out of the side pocket with one hand in under ten seconds while the other hand held the child. Crisis contained before the wailing hit cruising altitude. I have never moved faster with less.
 
1 p.m., she fell asleep standing up, the way they do. I carried thirty-four pounds of sweaty child on my shoulder AND drank my still-cold water while walking to our parade spot. Try that with a cup in your hand. You get to pick one child or hydration. I had both. I felt like a Marvel property.
 
3 p.m., Chris — who did not need anything like that — asked if I could "hold his bottle real quick." I looked at him with all the love of thirteen years of marriage and said no. He bought another Powerade. We don't talk about that either.
 
6 p.m., parade. A mom in the Dumbo line had her cup on the ground between her feet, hen position, and I swear she was me from two years ago. I pointed at my hip. She mouthed "where." I mouthed the name. We had a moment.
 
9 p.m., fireworks. My water was still cold. June in Orlando is a crockpot, and my water made it to the fireworks. I checked on the ice like it was a newborn. Still there.
 
Real talk so you don't come back mad at me: it's not the park bag. The park bag still exists — sunscreen, ponchos, the fourteen emergency items live there, and Chris carries it, which is the natural order. But every single thing I actually reached for between rope drop and fireworks lived on my hip.
 
If your cup has ever stood between your feet in a theme park line.
 
If you've ever handed a seven-year-old your phone and gotten eleven thumbs and a trash can.
 
If there's a trip on the calendar and you already know who ends up holding everything.
 
The buy one get one free is still running — summer sale. One for you, one for whoever does the parks with you. Not Chris though. Chris didn't need one.
 
Your hands are for the kids. The cup can ride.

Damon:You are not wolfless. They killed your wolf.

Today was Princess Marcy’s big day when the strongest Alpha was coming to woo her. The pack house was lavishly decorated. The Red Moon pack had spared no expenses to welcome Alpha Damon, the richest Alpha in North America. Important Alphas from all over had gathered and everyone looked festive expect me, So I decided to go back to my room in Dunegon. 
Marcy: “Talia, where do  you think you are going?”

I turned to see Marcy approaching with her servants. Even in her flowing white party dress, there was nothing gentle about her. Her blonde hair framed her perfect face, but her eyes were cold.

She demanded it like an accusation. I lowered my head, too intimidated to meet her gaze. She narrowed her eyes at me before cracking a smile that didn’t reach them.

Good. I wanna talk to you about something. I just
want to borrow the necklace you're wearing. It'll
go perfectly with the dress I plan to wear tonight to impress Damon.

“Sorry, but no.”

I refused without hesitation.

“This was my mother’s.”

Her gentle facade dropped instantly.

“Then don’t blame me. I need it.”

She signaled to her servants. Before I could react, they grabbed my arms and forced me to my knees.

“What are you doing?”

I gasped as Marcy yanked the necklace from my neck.

“Give me back my necklace. Stop!”

I cried out, struggling against their grip.

“You can’t do this. That’s all I have of her.”

Marcy struck me across the face with brutal force. I hit the ground hard. Pain exploded in my jaw. I tasted blood. My lip split wide open, and warm, thick blood poured down my chin. I clenched my fists, trembling with rage—but I was powerless.

Marcy was now going to be the Luna of our pack. Even if I wanted to fight back, what could I do? I was just a lone girl with no family, no power, no strength against the Alpha’s new bride.

Marcy reached down and held the necklace up to the light. I watched as the emeralds twinkled in her hand.

“Why do you need a servant’s necklace?” I asked her. “You are the princess of the Red Moon Pack. Surely you have many jewels to choose from.”

She sneered at me.

“You. This necklace is so cheap,” she said, examining it casually. “How could your mother leave you such a pathetic thing?”

Then she threw my necklace to the ground. The chain snapped instantly, the gems scattering across the floor.

“I am the daughter of a noble Alpha.”

She stepped on my hand as I tried to gather the pieces.

“Learn how to respect your new Luna.”

Tears burned at the corners of my eyes, but I forced them back. I wouldn’t give her the satisfaction. My cheek throbbed. The skin around my eye pulsed and burned—I could already feel the bruise forming, swelling.

Marcy stood there while I lay on the ground, bruised, battered, and utterly humiliated. Just then, the party music started. And Marcy rushed to change before Damon's arrival. 

Just then, the party music started. And marcy rused to change before Damon’s arrival

The moment Alpha Damon stepped onto Red Moon Pack grounds with his mated Betas, Caden and Maya, something felt off. His wolf stirred uneasily beneath the surface. Damon didn’t need confirmation, he already knew: no one in the Red Moon Pack could be trusted.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”

While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.

When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?

Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'

Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled.  In confirmation, I couldnt my wolf had been silenced years ago. 

My name is Talia, but no one calls me Talia except for teachers on the first day of schooling. I'm more popular as the wolfless freak. I'm a werewolf in the red moon pack. Since I'm an orphan, I'm not completely sure how old I am, but I'm pretty sure I'm 16. Also, I'm an omega, which means I'm a servant. My job is to make the meals for the werewolves who live in the pack house. Between making breakfast and dinner for over 100 wolves, cleaning up after them, and restocking the pantries of the ranked members' apartments on the 3rd and 4th floors, I do normal teenager stuff, except I don't have a lot of spare time to do so. Homework is the extent of living my teen life. Right now it's 11:30 at night. I'm putting the finishing touches on my English essay when I hear the door of the dungeon slam open. Great. Now what did I do? It doesn't take much. 
Alpha Edward is an alcoholic. It's really difficult for werewolves to get drunk, which means you have to drink heavily to feel the effects. This means he probably had a fight with Luna Layla about his drinking. Which means she locked him out of their room. Which means he has come down to take out his anger on me. Just an average Tuesday in the packhouse. I know the drill. I'm already on my feet waiting for him. I'm thinking in my mind. “Alpha Edward, what can I do for you?" I ask with my eyes looking at the floor. I keep my hands clasped in front of me, trying to look as small as possible. Without a word, a whiskey bottle whizzes past my ear and smashes against the wall above my cot. I flinch and can't help but start to tremble and hug myself. Whatever is about to happen it's going to be worse than usual. He lunges forward and grabs me by the throat with both hands. I feel tears coming to my eyes as the lack of oxygen turns the edges of my vision dark. I desperately claw at his hands, trying to escape his grip but it's no use. In the past couple of years, he started dipping the whip in wolfsbane, which makes me heal slower, so now I have gnarly scars across my back and arms. I managed to eke out. The lashes, combined with the glass shards still in my back, combined with the wolfbane are too much. My vision turns blurry and I pass out. Numbness surrounds me. Is this what being dead is like? It's peaceful, but a little bit boring. At least I don't have to feed the pack. I start to panic, making the beeps in the room become faster. Oh, I'm hooked up to a bunch of machines. I try to figure out how to unhook them so no one hears the noises. Too late, I hear people in the hallway getting closer. I try to sit up. I need to ignore the pain. I have to escape. I slowly slide off the side of the legs. My legs were wobbly. The tubes and wires sticking out of me prevent me from getting too far. The door opens and the pack doctor comes in with a nurse. The doctor is an older person. “Ah, Talia. You're awake. Let's get you back on the mat, shall we?" The doctor says gently. He and the nurse come to either side of me and reach out to hold my arms. A deep growl escapes my chest. “Don't touch me," I snap, shaking them off. My voice is scratchy and raw and my mouth feels like a thousand needles are poking into it. “Talia, you had surgery to remove hundreds of shards of glass from your back, we also had to reset some ribs, your jaw, and you had a lot of wolfsbane in your blood. We gave you a transfusion to clear it from your system so you could heal," the doctor explains, "You're lucky your wound isn’t badly serious.” Sure about that last part, doctor? I think to myself. “When the pack realized breakfast had not been prepared, Tony went to get you and found you on the ground in your...uh...room," he looked at me with sympathy, "Talia, who did this to you? It's a crime that could be grounds for banishment from the pack. Based on the scarring, this isn't the first time you've been attacked.” I can't answer him. I stare at my hands on my lap quietly. How can I tell him Alpha Edward is the one who caused this? There's no way he'd believe me, even if he did, what are they going to do? Banish the Alpha? Fat chance of that. I decide my best move is to just shake my head no. I don't want to get out of the pack for lying. I have nowhere to go. I would be nothing. “Okay. Let's move on to the next question. When do you turn seventeen?" He looks at the papers inside his folder. “I-I don't know exactly, sir," I say honestly. “M-my father brought me here when I was a baby. He was a bad guy. Alpha Edward, well...he..." I feel my face burning with embarrassment. My hands tremble and tears threaten to escape my eyes. I didn't think I would have to tell this story to the doctor. I thought everyone already knew. My father was a bad guy. Alpha Edward ended his life for coming into pack territory without permission. They didn't realize he was carrying a baby until they unzipped his jacket and saw I was tucked inside. It was a miracle I survived. Since I was just a baby, they couldn't just get rid of me but they didn't know anything about me. I was wrapped in a blanket that had the name 'Talia’' embroidered on it. So, that is what they called me. My father could have been a kidnapper for all I know. The only reason they gave me the last name Jackman is because after they took down my father, they looked through his wallet to identify him. The only form of ID he had was a library card that said Brian Jackman on it. I've tried an internet search for his name on the computer in the school library before. Nothing comes up in the search. “You don't need to finish, I know what happened to your father.” “Well, after that...happened...Luna Layla took me in until I was old enough to start school. Then she moved me into the dungeon. I've kinda been on my own since then. I never found out when my actual birthday was. To be honest, you're the first person who has ever asked. I mean, I guess I'm sixteen. My wolf hasn't woken up yet.” The doctor nods, looking at me with pity. Almost like he cares. He asks me a few more questions about my medical history, but there's nothing to speak of. I don't remember ever being treated by a doctor before. “I see," he closes the folder and tucks his pen into his shirt pocket, "Well, I know you haven't had a chance to look in the mirror yet, but when you do, you may find you look a little different. Don't be alarmed. I've done as many tests as I could think of. It is not medically related.” I look at him with confusion, "Y-yes, sir." I assume he means I'm healing faster but, why did he need me to look in the mirror? Why not just tell me? I look at the nurse who is staring at me. When she realizes I caught her, her eyes dart away. What's that about? Okay, lady. Rude. “I'll leave you now," she says, "You can go in the bathroom and wash up. Just take that pole with the IV solution with you. There are lounge shorts and fresh underwear in the bag. You need to leave the hospital gown on until your back heals. Alright?” “Yes, ma'am. Thank you, Diane," she nods and leaves the room. It's the first time in my life people have been kind to me. I mean, I think it's part of their job but still. All I have known so far were insults, physical misery, and hard work. Never any kindness, never any. Everything in the bathroom is fresh. There's a shower, but I'm worried the pressure of the water will hurt my back. I decided to fill the tub halfway and get in. The water is warm and soothing. There's a washcloth and a fresh bar of soap. I clean myself until the water is gross. I drain the tub, wipe out the ring of dirt around the edge, and fill it again. The water is not nearly as dirty as this time when I finish washing. I find it hard to raise my hands, but I don't want to call the nurse to help me. I gently wash my hair, dry off and wrap the soft towel around my head. There's a toothbrush and a small tube of paste on the shelf by the sink. I'm living in the lap of luxury in the pack hospital! I pick them up and start brushing my teeth. I can't avoid it anymore, I need to look in the mirror. I finally worked up the courage to take a peek. What I see makes me drop the toothbrush. My face is still covered in bruises, but that's not what made me drop the toothbrush. The iris of my left eye is violet. No. My right pupil is still the drab gray I'm used to but my left pupil looks crazy. I blink my eyes hard a few times. Still the same. I tried rubbing my eye but it doesn't make a difference. There's no mistaking it - my eye is bright, practically glowing...violet. The two days seem to last forever. I'm not complaining though. I've never gotten so much in my life and as a bonus, I get three meals a day. Three! I keep looking in the mirror. I can't get over how weird my purple eye looks. I wake up on the second day and go to the bathroom to freshen up. I stare at myself in the mirror for the millionth time. My left eye is still violet. Now my right eye seems like it's starting to turn violet as well. There was nothing I could do about it, so I decided to try not to worry. Since Red Moon is a pretty big pack, we have a high school on pack territory. The library has a really big werewolf lore research section. I will do some research during lunch. As I tilt my head to the side to brush my hair, I notice a chunk of my hair has changed color. Instead of my normal mousy brown, it is silvery gray. Okay seriously now. What is going on? What is happening to me? Is this a trick? Is there bleach in the shampoo or something? If it is a trick, it isn't funny. I pick up the bottle and smell it. It smells like strawberries, not bleach. Weird. I have never heard of a wolf's eye or hair color changing when they are coming of age but that's what the doctor thinks is happening. Diane comes in just after lunch with paperwork and pamphlets for me. She hands me another little bag, "Just a little something to help you stay incognito until you are finished healing," she says. "Thank you for everything," I say as I open the bag. There is a baseball cap and a pair of dark sunglasses. "How do I look?" I ask as I model them for her. She giggles at my poses, "You're a star, darling." Maybe she isn't so bad after all. She gives me a gentle hug and sends me on my way. I have another two hours before I need to start prepping dinner. I decided to take my new clothes to my room and clean up the mess down there so I can tonight. Something smells different as I walk down the hall of the dungeon, like a cleaning solution. I turn on my lamp to find the room has been transformed. My lamp is not sitting on an old stack of milk crates. It is on a nightstand. There is a new one too, my old cot is gone. I have a proper. Complete with new sheets and blankets. There is also a small desk and chair with all my school books arranged in a basket next to it. I must be dreaming. That or I walked into someone else's room by accident, except no one else lives down here. You can barely tell it was an old dungeon cell. It looks like what I imagine a dorm room would look like. I peek out of the doorway to make sure I am in the right place. I seem to be. What gives? I walk over and sit carefully as if it will disappear if I move too fast. It is like a cloud. The gray and turquoise linens are fresh and new. There are even two pillows. I never had a proper pillow before, let alone two. As far as I know, Diane is the only one who came down here while I was in the hospital. Could she have had all this done? Surely she will get in trouble when Alpha Edward finds out. Then I remember she doesn't know how much the Alpha hates me. I don't know how I'm going to explain it when he finds out but I won't tattle on anyone for trying to help me either. I put my new clothes away in the drawers of the nightstand. I stash the duffle bag under the mattress. Once I am seventeen, I will figure out a way to get out of this place. Find a new pack that will accept a violet-eyed weakling of a wolf. I sit at the desk and write a thank you letter to the doctor and Nurse Diane. I turn in the chair looking around the like-new room. I am in awe that someone would do this for me. I must have been daydreaming because I don't hear the door at the top of the stairs, but I hear two sets of footsteps coming down the hall. Instantly I freeze. I can smell Alpha Edward's scent getting closer. I don't know who the other scent belongs to. Instinctively, I scramble and stand in the middle of the room just as they get to the doorway. He leans against the frame and crosses his arms in front of himself. I can feel my whole trembling as he stares. My eyes are glued to the ground. I do not want him to see my new eye color shining through. "C-can I help y-you, Alpha Edward?" "That little stunt you pulled cost me a lot of money," he says with a calm, gravelly voice, "And when you cost me money, you cost my whole family money." "I'm sorry, sir," I apologize, although I have no idea what stunt he is talking about. I look up just enough to see Marcy, the Alpha's daughter, is also standing in the doorway. Marcy takes a step closer and I can feel tears starting to sting the corners of my eyes as my arms shake uncontrollably. How am I going to face her at school? I haven't had a conversation with her since her mom made me live in the dungeon, anyway. But as far as I know, she had no idea I live down here now. She is going to tell everyone for sure. "Surgery and hospital stays aren't cheap, Talia," Alpha Edward sneers from the doorway, "And do you know how disgusting the food has been for the past two and a half days?" I just nod, still looking at the ground. I'm not trying to argue with a lunatic. It isn't my fault I had to have surgery. He's the one who broke a bottle and threw me into the broken pieces! If he hadn't, I would have been just fine. I would have been able to bounce back the next day and make breakfast like I was supposed to, even if I was banged up. There is a pause and he finally growls, "Where did all this furniture come from? Did you steal it?” “N-no, sir. I-I...it was here when I g-got back from the hospital wing. I don't know wh-who brought it.” "You owe me, Talia. You also owe whoever turned your room into this comfortable space. You'll work in the packhouse until you pay it back every cent. For the rest of your life if necessary. No more school. You don't need education to cook and clean." He uses his Alpha tone. I cannot disobey. With those words, the small flame of hope in my heart extinguishes. I don't get paid so I don't know how I could ever pay back any debt. Luna Layla told me years ago that the room in the dungeon was payment enough for my services. I am less than an omega now. I am a slave. "Marcy, teach her a lesson for wasting our money." "Yes, Alpha.” Tears stream down my face as the reality of my fate sets in. Alpha Edward is passing the torch of his cruelty down to his daughter. But I know better than that. He will never stop. Marcy reaches forward and claps the back of my neck. She forces me down into a bowing position and growls deeply, "You should be grateful my father doesn't banish you. If you were a rogue, I would make sure you never made it to the border of the territory." A squeak escapes my throat. I am so scared I feel like I am going to pass out. Marcy turns to her father, "Don't worry, Alpha. I've got this situation covered." I hear Alpha Edward's footsteps walk back down the hallway as he leaves the dungeon. Marcy tightens her grip on my neck, extending her wolf claws, making me yelp. As soon as the door slams, Marcy releases my neck and kneels in front of me. Her face is contorted with anger. She grabs my shoulders, shaking me roughly, "What did you do to make him so mad?" Why isn't she doing anything to me like she told Alpha Edward she would? I stiffened my whole body, avoiding eye contact with her. I'm shaking, I can't even speak now. The thought of two people doing something bad to me regularly for the rest of my life...it just can't be real. Can it? How can the Moon Goddess allow this to happen? I want to leave the world. That's not an exaggeration. That's not me being dramatic. Please, Moon Goddess, don't let this happen. Just let me go. I shake so badly that I fall to my knees. Luna Layla keeps taking his glass away from him, but he keeps ordering the omegas to give him more. The dining room is extra crowded, so I don't get a better look at Alpha Damon. Maya sees me peeking out from the kitchen and gives me a wink and thumbs up. I smile and give a little wave before pulling my head back. I help the servers take the party food to the tables at the edges of the ballroom. I also make sure the bars in the corners are fully stocked. The DJ is finishing setting up and colorful lights are sliding across the floor. Party balloons and streamers are hanging all over the place. The first few guests are starting to wander in which is my cue to duck out the back door. Luckily, the dinner servers will clean up the dinner service tonight, which gives me extra time to restock pantries. I head upstairs to the stockroom and load the cart up. I'm humming to myself as I go from room to room. I feel an odd sense of calm as I go. "You're in a good mood," Sylvie  says. "I guess. I'm not sure why though. My back and feet still make me feel bad. " "Well, I'm happy that you're happy for once. This version of you is pretty cool." "Thanks,  Sylvie . You're not half bad yourself." I finish stocking the ranked pack members' rooms on the fourth and third floors. Then head to the second floor where the guest suites are. The cleaning staff has cleaned the rooms and bathrooms. I just need to restock the toiletries, pantry items, and refrigerators. I make quick work of the rooms. I remember to stock the Betas' room with more bottles of San Pellegrino, refresh the flowers, and leave a little tent card with a handwritten smiley face on the kitchenette counter. 

It was almost midnight by the time I was wrapping up, and everyone was still in the ballroom. 

I closed the door to the Beta's suite and moved on to the Alpha's suite door. 

It's the last room left. He must be at the party too, but I knocked before entering just in case.

I put my ear against the door and heard nothing, so I slipped my key in the lock and opened the door, but the moment I looked inside, my heart stopped, and I froze. 

Standing there was the most handsome werewolf I've ever seen in my life.

Easily six foot, six inches tall, looked to be about two hundred fifty pounds of solid muscle with the broadest shoulders, but he wasn’t alone, an icy Blonde stood in front of him with her hands undoing his belt.

The smell of coffee and dark chocolate filled the air, and my mind went hazy as I froze, seeing two piercing blue eyes staring back at me. 

"Stop!" He shouted.

'Is this it? Is this the day I die?' I wondered.
